skills_considered.reason: The discovery ledger is a research surface owned by other batches; the one ledger correction this reading supports is proposed through the intake note rather than edited.
A patient genotype-phenotype report supplies no therapeutic lever for the reference genotype class; forging hypotheses from one case would manufacture a lead.
No compound is tested as an intervention with a measured outcome beyond clinical anecdote, so there is no molecule to send to BLOCK-1 triage.
Scientists do not touch the four current files; every change is proposed as a commit candidate for a later BATCH_COMMIT.
The triples are published in the candidates for a blind auditor; the reader of a paper cannot audit their own locators.

group_assessment.weighting: PubMed counts 2026-10-02: Bolz HJ[au] 113, Bolz HJ[au] AND WWOX 1 (this paper). A clinical/molecular genetics group (retinal and syndromic genetics) reporting one consanguineous family. The sequencing observation is credible; the human-rat convergence and the carrier tumour statements are interpretation over one family.

entries.proposition: The body gives the nonsense allele as c.160G > T; on NM_016373.4 position c.160 is C (codon 54 = CGA), so G>T is inconsistent with an arginine codon.
entries.snippet: affects codon 54 for arginine (c.160G > T; p.Arg54*)

entries.proposition: The authors' own deposited Additional file 1 (IGV slide) labels the same variant c.160C>T, contradicting the body's c.160G>T.
Only one affected child was genotyped; the elder affected sib was never seen by the authors and is counted as probably affected.
entries.snippet: Patient II:1 died several years ago and has not been seen by the authors

entries.proposition: Seizures in the genotyped child responded partially to two drugs; the paper does not report drug resistance to all agents.
entries.snippet: Seizures partially responded to valproate and lamotrigine.

entries.proposition: Survival endpoint of the genotyped homozygote.
entries.snippet: II:4 died at the age of 16 months because of status epilepticus.

entries.proposition: The metabolic screen is blood/urine chemistry; no muscle biopsy or mitochondrial study is named in the list.
entries.snippet: Normal results were found in metabolic screening including liver and renal function tests

entries.proposition: The no-tumour statement for carriers is an observation to date, not a negative for carrier risk.
entries.snippet: No tumors have developed so far in the heterozygous carriers in our family

entries.proposition: The authors themselves consider an increased lifetime cancer risk in carriers conceivable.
entries.snippet: However, an increased cumulative lifetime risk, especially if exposed to carcinogenic agents, seems conceivable

entries.proposition: Causality rests on homozygosity by descent; the authors state they cannot exclude a compound heterozygous cause elsewhere.
entries.snippet: we can not exclude disease-causing compound heterozygosity in a gene outside the HBD regions

entries.proposition: The protein-null statement in Table 1 is about the rat allele, carried from the rat literature; no human protein or RNA assay is reported.
MRI findings in the genotyped child are cortical/hippocampal/callosal; the cerebellum is not annotated.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2 A-C: coronal FLAIR with thin cortex and hippocampal dysplasia arrows; sagittal T1 with hypoplastic corpus callosum; axial T2 with temporal hypotrophy and widened subarachnoid space. No cerebellar annotation.
